etymologies.etymologyHTML: The word is first known in English from the 17th century as a borrowing from Middle Scots golf, gouff. Although the etymology is uncertain, the most likely origin is that it comes from the Middle Dutch colve, colf (“club”), ultimately from Proto-Germanic *kulbaz (“club”), related to German Kolben (“piston, rod”), Swedish kolv (“piston, rod”), Old English clopp (“rock; cliff”).

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To play the game of golf.

quote.citation: 1894, Rudyard Kipling, The Day's Work/An Error in the Fourth Dimension:
quote.text: Last mystery of all, he learned to golf.

definitions.definition: (computing) To write something in as few characters as possible (e.g. in code golf, regex golf)
